editorialNotes.basis: Hyman, Vol. 3, p. 1071 (right column). The רבה בר איסי entry ends "ואולי הוא" ("and perhaps he is") with no complement. The next printed heading, "רבה בר איתי", is the only heading on the page without a closing period, and its text opens with the relative "שהיה" ("who was"), then returns to Sotah 30a, the one citation in the רבה בר איסי entry. Hebrew Wikisource's editor footnotes the same place: "המשך המשפט בערך הבא". Read together: "perhaps he is Rabba bar Itai, who was in Rav's time (see Rava bar Itai); and in Sotah 30a too read 'Rabba bar Itai', and this needs investigation (וצ״ע)". Hyman's identification is tentative. This entry's text is kept exactly as printed. Its opening "שהיה" continues "ואולי הוא" at the end of the רבה בר איסי entry, where the joined sentence is shown.

editorialNotes.beforeStatus: Printed reading retained; possible misprint flagged, not corrected.
editorialNotes.basis: The print clearly reads "אמר רבה". Sotah 30a:3 has "אמר רבה בן איסי אמר רב", the רבה בר איסי entry says "אמר רב", and this entry places רבה בר איתי "בזמן רב", so "רבה" may be a misprint for "רב". That is an inference about Hyman's intent, not a reading of the page. רבה בר איתי has no Talmud attestation of his own; he exists here only through Hyman's tentative correction of Sotah 30a.
